sentences.text: Strigops insulaborealis was described by Worthy and colleagues.
The species lived during the Pleistocene epoch.
Its fossils were recovered in New Zealand.
It is an extinct parrot closely related to the kākāpō.
The specific epithet references that the holotype—the specimen on which the species is based—was discovered on New Zealand's North Island.
Worthy et al. formally named the species in 2026.
The genus Strigops is placed in the family Strigopidae.
Strigops insulaborealis inhabited Zealandia during the Calabrian stage of the Pleistocene.
The genus Strigops persisted from the Late Pleistocene to the Holocene, spanning from 0.129 million years ago to the present.
